messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 paging: high-rate GPU driver resets observed in cluster infer-prod-3 (node infer-prod-3-17). Metric spike: nvml_driver_reset_count + container restarts. Alerts: https://telemetry.redwood/alerts/5309991111 :rotating_light:
Samira (oncall): taking this. tagging infra/eng-runtime. ETA 2m to triage.
Jae Park: seeing repeated driver hot-reset messages in kernel logs and containers OOMing during KV cache build. snippet:```kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=10234, 0x00000000``` also `nvidia-smi` shows GPU0 ECC corrected count jumping ~80->120 in last 15m.
Mei Chen: confirm ECC-correctable surge on GPU0, GPU1 stable. `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` output noisy. suspect intermittent memory errors triggering driver resets.
Nate: recommended immediate mitigation: cordon + drain infer-prod-3-17, and shift inference traffic to other pool. Also open a support bridge for customers if 5xxs.
Carlos: executing cordon now: `kubectl cordon infer-prod-3-17` -> node cordoned. preparing drain with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` to accelerate.
Samira (oncall): @channel please post any customer-facing errors. I see increased 503s for model-run endpoints (embed/stream). @support escalate to customers with impact window. :warning:
ops-bot: Automated fallback activated -> route requests for model-x to model-x-variant-b in us-west-2 while node evacuation completes.
Carlos: drain kicked off. Some pods failed to terminate due to local kvcache files. Forced delete of pods holding local disk: `kubectl delete pod ... --grace-period=0`
Jae Park: copying kernel excerpt from crashed container for ops log:
```
[ 12345.678901] oom-killer: kill process 23456 (python) score 123 or sacrifice child
[ 12345.679002] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=23456, GPU has fallen off the bus
```
Mei Chen: tried `nvidia-smi --gpu-reset -i 0` but it failed - hardware not in a resettable state remotely. Looks like driver reload won't stick: `modprobe nvidia` throws errors.
Nate: since remote reset failed, plan B: reboot node after eviction. coordinating reboot now. datacenter team FYI in case there's hardware flakiness.
datacenter-oncall: acknowledge, we'll monitor during reboot and prepare for hardware swap if persistent.
Carlos: node rebooting. status: kubelet removed node, pods rescheduled.
Samira (oncall): Customer impact: Support ticket aggregator shows ~12 affected customers with transient 5xxs, highest degradation between 12:03-12:12 UTC. Notifying CS to update status page.
ops-bot: Rolling traffic back to primary model variants once replica counts normalized.
Jae Park: After reboot, node came up but `dmesg` shows multiple memory ECC corrected events and then driver reset during driver probe:```
[    8.123456] amdgpu? no, but nvme? NVRM: GPU at PCI:65:00 ECC correctable count 180 -> 260
[   10.654321] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, GPU reset
```
Mei Chen: this is recurring on the same GPU index (GPU0). We've isolated it to a board-level fault—requests to datacenter for physical reseat or RMA.
Nate: temporary operational mitigations: 1) label node `gpu=degraded` and taint `gpu=isolated:NoSchedule`; 2) cordon permanently and redeploy capacity from auto-scaling group; 3) add an alert on ECC-correctable-rate to trigger auto-evac at threshold.
Carlos: applied taint and label, and drained remaining workloads off core GPUs. Confirmed no further restarts on other nodes.
Samira (oncall): escalated to hardware RMA. opened ticket DCR-9482 with datacenter and hardware vendor. Posting link: https://dcops/tickets/DCR-9482
datacenter-oncall: vendor scheduled engineer on-site in next maintenance window; interim step: we removed GPU0 from host via BMC soft-disable to prevent auto-reload attempts.
Mei Chen: telemetry note: we saw progressive ECC correctables followed by uncorrectable attempts? no UCEs logged yet but pattern matches failing DIMM or GPU memory bus.
Jae Park: customer bridge open: https://bridges.redwood/5309991111 (support + infra + eng-runtime).
Samira (oncall): current status: node offline, workloads healthy on fallback nodes, customer impact reduced to intermittent slowdowns. P1 -> P2 for monitoring.
Carlos: postmortem action items I'm adding: 1) auto-evac on ECC rate threshold; 2) improve pod eviction for local-kvcache workloads (faster fallback); 3) document runbook for remote GPU soft-disable.
Mei Chen: will bake change to telemetry: add moving-window ECC slope alert and integrate with autoscaler to avoid single-GPU hotspots.
Nate: also recommend sched policy change to prefer spreading KV-heavy pods across GPUs to avoid correlated OOM.
Samira (oncall): thanks team. I'll hand this off to eng-runtime for follow up. closing incident channel once hardware RMA confirms. :white_check_mark:
